questions.question: Which of the following is a best practice for handling form validation in Django? Choose all that apply.
options: A. Use Django's built-in form classes
B. Override the form's clean method to add custom validation
C. Use Django's form validation directly without custom methods
D. Use JavaScript to validate forms on the client side
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use Django's built-in form classes and override the form's clean method for custom validation.

questions.question: In Django, what is the primary difference between using Django's built-in authentication system and writing custom authentication logic?
options: A. Built-in authentication is slower but more secure
B. Built-in authentication is easier to set up and secure
C. Built-in authentication is more flexible and secure
D. Built-in authentication is less secure and harder to set up
questions.explanation: Built-in authentication in Django is easier to set up and secure, provided you use the provided signals and middleware.

questions.question: Which Django feature is used to securely store user passwords and ensure they are not stored in plain text?
options: A. Django's built-in authentication system
B. Django's form validation
C. Django's form handling
D. Django's database migrations
questions.explanation: Django's built-in authentication system uses Django's User model, which includes a secure method for storing passwords using the `set_password` method.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common method to handle form errors in Django without using Django's built-in form handling classes?
options: A. Use Django's form validation directly
B. Use Django's form handling classes
C. Use JavaScript to handle errors on the client side
D. Use Django's custom form handling classes
questions.explanation: Handling form errors on the client side using JavaScript is a common method to provide a better user experience without relying on Django's form handling classes.

questions.question: In Django, what is the purpose of the `@login_required` decorator in views?
options: A. To require users to be logged in to access the view
B. To require users to be logged out to access the view
C. To require users to be authenticated to access the view
D. To require users to be unauthenticated to access the view
questions.explanation: The `@login_required` decorator in Django is used to ensure that users must be authenticated to access the view.
